title: ForestBench: A Unified Graph Framework for Evaluating Multi-Agent Collaboration
summary:
The paper addresses the lack of a common basis for comparing heterogeneous LLM-based multi-agent system (MAS) execution traces. Outcome-only benchmarks such as GSM8K, MMLU, and HumanEval reduce a run to a final answer and discard collaboration. LLM-as-Judge evaluation requires additional, model- and rubric-dependent inference and has limited reproducibility.

ForestBench maps native MAS traces into directed acyclic collaboration graphs, where nodes are agent actions and edges encode communicative or information-flow dependencies. Each query has a reference forest of ten precomputed, verified-success graphs from six representative MAS paradigms plus a single-agent anchor, so no single coordination style is treated as the gold process. A deterministic metric panel scores candidates on structure, information uptake, redundancy, and cost, with the headline Forest Match metric measuring alignment with the forest. The benchmark contains 844 collaboration-necessary queries filtered from seven public datasets.
